title: MAT Dominator Tree 与 Retained Heap 解读
key_conclusions: A dominator is an object that every path from GC roots to another object must pass through; the immediate dominator is the closest mandatory owner.
Retained heap is the theoretical reclaimable impact if an object becomes unreachable, while shallow heap is only the object's own size.
Dominator Tree ranks impact, and Path To GC Roots proves ownership; reliable leak decisions require both views plus lifecycle semantics.
Large retained heap can be a real leak, a bounded cache, a bitmap pool, a session owner, a thread queue, or a classloader boundary, so cache policy and external metrics must be checked.
shallow_points: The article still explains retained heap with representative object graphs rather than exporting a real MAT dominator tree.
